_comment: PUBLISHED packages: @arthome/core and @arthome/contracts. READ BY TYPESCRIPT 6 ONLY.
This is the one file in the setup that TypeScript 7 never reads, because the two
published packages are built with typescript@6.0.3 — the floor of their consumers.
So this is where, and only where, stableTypeOrdering goes.
stableTypeOrdering — TypeScript assigns type ids in the order it meets types and
sorts unions by those ids: adding a const above a function can REVERSE the order of
a union in the emitted .d.ts, without a single line of the type having changed.
TypeScript 7 sorts deterministically; this option makes TypeScript 6 adopt that same
ordering. Published .d.ts files become reproducible AND are already what 7.0 would
emit. Cost: up to 25% more checking — acceptable on two rarely built packages,
On the day we move to TypeScript 7: this line disappears, and that is all.
isolatedDeclarations — refuses any export whose type cannot be written without
inferring through the function body. This is the real guarantee that a .d.ts is
'readable by both compilers': the public surface is annotated, so it depends on no
inference subtlety. Errors surface at the publisher, not at the consumer.
outDir, rootDir, include and exclude belong to the package's tsconfig.build.json.
